story.title: Apple Unveils Touch-Screen MacBook Pro, Reversing Jobs’ Stance - Bloomberg

facts.text: Bloomberg News first reported in January 2023 that Apple was working on a touch-screen MacBook Pro.
For the revamped MacBook Pro, Apple is retiring the “notch” — the cutout at the top of the screen that houses the camera.
The current MacBook Pro design dates back to 2021, though Apple refreshed the 14-inch base version with an M5 chip on Wednesday.
The late Jobs, then Apple’s chief executive officer, said in 2010 that “touch surfaces don’t want to be vertical,” suggesting that they wouldn’t make sense for a computer screen.
As of now, Apple isn’t actively developing additional touch-screen Macs.
There have been concerns within Apple that touch-screen computers would cannibalize sales of iPads.
While the $999 MacBook Air remains the company’s bestselling laptop, a high-end touch-enabled MacBook Pro might entice customers to trade up — or switch from a Windows PC.
Apple’s iPad Magic Keyboard, introduced in 2020, also showed that customers were interested in combining a touch display with a traditional keyboard and trackpad.
Apple is exploring another major Mac change as well: a shift from the Touch ID fingerprint scanner to Face ID.
Apple shares pared their losses Thursday after Bloomberg reported on the plans.
The company is planning M5 Pro and M5 Max iterations for early 2026 that retain the current look, Bloomberg News has reported.
The company has also developed a reinforced hinge and screen hardware to prevent the display from bouncing back or moving when touched, a common drawback of existing touch PCs.
This follows a typical strategy for Apple, which offers new features on its top-end devices before bringing them down-market.
But tablet growth has already slowed in recent years, and touch screens have increasingly become must-have features for PCs.

After two decades of spurning the idea, Apple Inc. unveiled an overhauled MacBook Pro that includes a touch screen, giving its flagship laptop a feature that has become a must-have in the personal computer industry.

(Bloomberg) -- After two decades of spurning the idea, Apple Inc. unveiled an overhauled MacBook Pro that includes a touch screen, giving its flagship laptop a feature that has become a must-have in the personal computer industry.

Co-founder Steve Jobs famously lambasted touch Macs in the later stages of his career, once calling them “ergonomically terrible.” Cook, his successor, said combining a laptop and tablet would be like merging a fridge and toaster.
Customers have been prodding the company for years to embrace touch displays, which the iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch helped popularize.

It’s also the first Mac with a Dynamic Island, the screen element familiar to iPhone users.The computer has a redesigned software interface optimized for touch and is offered with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

The launches cap a strong new product year for Apple, which put the iPhone Duo on sale last Friday. (Updated with more product details starting in third paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.
Apple unveiled the first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen in Mac history.
After 20 years of refusing to add a touchscreen since the MacBook's 2006 launch, Apple changed course under new CEO John Turnus.
Apple founder Steve Jobs once said, "Touchscreen notebooks are ergonomically terrible."
Apple had long been negative about adding touchscreens to laptops.

2010, founder Jobs said, "Touch surfaces don't want to be vertical," adding, "After a short period, you start to fatigue, and after an extended period, your arm wants to fall off." He called them "ergonomically terrible" and kept touchscreens off the Mac.
The 14-inch model of the touchscreen MacBook Pro weighs 1.38 kg, down 220 g from its predecessor, and the 16-inch model weighs 1.82 kg, 320 g lighter, improving portability.
Unified memory goes up to 128GB, and storage up to 16TB.
Apple will begin preorders today in 30 countries, including the United States, and on the 30th in Korea.
Apple said it reduced latency by integrating the touch sensor into the panel itself rather than placing it on top of the display.
